title: Stateful change guard with probationary canary and cost-aware throttles
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a stateful change-guard that applies configuration changes through a probationary canary window and enforces cost-aware throttles. The guard should track per-model and per-tenant prefix/KV cache coherence, maintain lightweight snapshots for safe rollback, and apply hysteresis to avoid thrashing. Goal: reduce risk of config-induced regressions (cost and latency) while enabling automated reversion when economic or correctness safeguards trip.
acceptance_criteria: New config changes can be deployed in probationary mode (canary) for a configurable window without impacting global traffic
If cost or correctness signals exceed thresholds during probation, the system automatically reverts the change for affected shards and records a reversible snapshot
KV cache coherence checks ensure no key-space divergence after apply; divergence triggers quarantine of cache and rollback for affected prefixes
Throttles are applied based on a cost budget per deployment so that rollback decisions account for cost delta and latency SLO violation likelihood
Automatic rollback provides an explainable reason and a link to the snapshot and diagnostics in the rollback event
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Instrumentation - emit metric facets for cost-per-token, per-prefix cache-hit-rate, and apply-latency delta
Phase 2: Probationary canary runner - add a canary routing policy and probation window state machine
Phase 3: Snapshotting - lightweight state snapshot API for config and cache metadata (not full blob) to support targeted rollback
Phase 4: Rollback controller - evaluate signals, compute confidence score, and execute targeted rollback with quarantine and thaw policies
Phase 5: Observability and runbook - add console view with one-click inspect, rollback reason, and PRD/design links
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positive rollbacks from noisy cost signals. Mitigation: implement smoothing/hysteresis and minimum sample windows before triggering auto-revert.
Risk: Rollback leaves KV cache inconsistent across shards. Mitigation: targeted prefix quarantine and reconcile job that replays safe prefetch checkpoints.
Risk: Rollback triggers cascading failover across capacity pools. Mitigation: include capacity-awareness in rollback planner and rate-limit rollback concurrency.
testing_plan: Unit tests for probationary state transitions and confidence scoring
Staging canary run with synthetic QPS patterns including cost spikes, cold cache, and sustained latency degradation
Chaos test: simulate partial apply failures and KV divergence, verify quarantine and reconcile path
E2E test: fail open vs. fail closed scenarios and operator override for emergency rollback
notes: This feature sits adjacent to the batching/caching recommender: some config changes may be suggested by Optimize; this guard ensures suggested changes are safe to apply at scale.
Prefer small, targeted snapshots (config + prefix hashes + cache metrics) instead of entire cache dumps to keep rollback latency low.
We will reuse existing rollout infra but add a probation flag and a rollback reasoning payload schema for audit logs.
open_questions: How long should default probation windows be for Dedicated vs Hosted tiers? (Recommend 15m for Hosted, 60m for Dedicated to allow larger traffic smoothing)
What confidence threshold balances speed vs. risk for auto-revert? (Initial proposal: score >= 0.85 based on multiple signals)
Should rollback controller attempt a graded rollback (only affected prefixes) before global revert? (Yes, prefer minimal blast radius.)
